title: Playing for the cabaret acts and joining Armand Piron's eight-piece band
summary: The casino's backers, white acts and the hurt feelings with Roy Palmer and Baby Dodds; he lists Piron's band lineup and later takes it over.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Eddie Grossell's Casino. Yeah. You can put that down if you want. And he had, his partner was Del Peter, and his manager was a German Jew, Mr. Hunts. Hunts was his name. And everything was run through transportation of the theaters and all the Spokin people that came in town to shows. Like every show would come to the Crescent Theater or Tulane, don't care if it was, those two theaters sat right together, the Crescent and Tulane, the Opera House, and don't care what sort of show it was, they'd go get those people at night and bring them there and have parties for them. And all the acts that we used in the place was white. Well we got so in a little while after I was there that we played practically all the white acts. Don't care what sort of music they brought in there. If I thought I couldn't play it, if there was a man who thought he couldn't play it, we had an eight piece band. If I thought we couldn't play it, we'd lay down low, or play low where we couldn't. Yeah. Get by with it. In that band, it seemed like that Baby Dutch, Roy Palmer, and all those, that's where the little bad feelings come in there. Because I left that band and went into an organized band. Well the boys wanted me to help them, well I couldn't take Baby Dutch and that because this, Armand J.P. Rons had a band before I went there, see. And naturally they put me in the band and commenced to giving me charge right away and teaching me and everything about the band. That band, that was my second band, that band consists of eight pieces. There was Armand J.P. Rons on violin, George P. Emerson on piano, Archie Walls on bass, Wade Whaley on clarinet.
Willie Hightower on trumpet, Elvin Zoo Roberson on trombone. Way left that band went to Oak, Oakland, California.
He played with Ory and Mud Carey and some of that. Yeah, that's right.

He played with Ory and Mud Carey there. But he didn't depend on music too much because he was a decorator. He decorated. But he was a very independent little fellow. He bought a home there, see, in the Uptown, up by Protection Levy. And that band, I stayed with that band two years and seven months. Armand J.P. Rons band, until P. Rons got a job at the St. Charles Hotel. And he took four pieces, or five pieces over there, and turned this band over to me. But he didn't take no man out of this band. He used all string over there in the St. Charles Hotel. I forget now, was it the Gold Room or something? Gold Room, I think it was, and he played in. Well, I kept that band for two years and seven months. And what upset the thing was, somebody come into New York, a performer, scouting around, and they heard of me, and they wanted to hear me play. And that man was, his name was Alexander Tolliver. He was with the Smart Setson. Mr. Parks, what was Parks' name?
